comment: Model selection is declared here so 'which model' is one frozen experiment
input rather than a value buried in three different harness config files.
Switching the active profile changes model identity STRENGTH as well as the
model: a local model is content-addressed by digest, while a gateway model is
only a label the gateway promises to honour and may silently reroute.
Record the strength; do not pretend a gateway label is a digest.
Upstream llama.cpp llama-server (v0.9.0) on loopback, started with --jinja
and --alias qwen3.8:27b. llama.cpp exposes no digest, so model_digest is the
SHA-256 that names the served GGUF: the model layer of Ollama's public
qwen3.8:27b (Q4_K_M), or any byte-identical copy named by its hash.
OpenCode Go serves OpenAI-compatible models at /chat/completions;
MiniMax and Qwen are Anthropic-compatible (/messages) and Grok and
GPT 5.6 Luna use /responses, so only the /chat/completions family is
usable by both DeepSeek Harness and Hermes without new provider code.

Hermes's 'custom' provider authenticates from OPENAI_API_KEY, while DeepSeek's llm-pi-ai reads the apiKeyEnv named in its patch. subject_key_env records that difference instead of hiding it in adapter code.
